items.title: Russia sharing intelligence with Iran to target US forces, officials say

featured_image.name: Russia, Iran sign military cooperation deal

items.description:
Russia has been providing Iran with targeting information on American military assets in the Middle East since the war erupted on February 28, according to a Washington Post report citing three U.S. officials familiar with the intelligence. The assistance includes real-time data on the locations of U.S. warships and aircraft, marking the first indication that another major American adversary is indirectly involved in the conflict.[1]

"It does seem like it's a pretty comprehensive effort," one official told the Washington Post.[2][3]

items.title: Iran war costs nearly $900M a day as oil hits 2-year high

featured_image.name: Oil prices surge because of Iran war : NPR

items.description: One week into the U.S.-Israeli military campaign against Iran, oil prices have climbed to their highest levels in nearly two years, rattling global markets and raising urgent questions about the economic toll of a widening Middle East conflict. Brent crude surged roughly 25% from pre-war levels to trade near $85 a barrel, while West Texas Intermediate rose to the upper $70s, as Iran's effective closure of the Strait of Hormuz choked off a shipping lane that carries about 20% of the world's oil supply.[1][2][3]

items.title: Trump demands 'unconditional surrender' as Iran war enters Day 7

featured_image.name: Trump says there will be no deal with Iran except 'unconditional surrender'

items.description:
The US-Israeli military campaign against Iran showed no signs of abating on March 6, 2026, as Israel launched heavy airstrikes on Tehran and Beirut overnight while Iran continued retaliatory strikes on Israel, American military bases, and Gulf state capitals. Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth said the conflict has "only just commenced," while President Trump declared on Truth Social that there would be "no deal with Iran except UNCONDITIONAL SURRENDER".[1][2]

The war, now in its seventh day, has killed more than 1,000 civilians in Iran alone, according to the US-based Human Rights Activists News Agency, which reported 1,097 civilian deaths including 181 children under the age of 10. An Iranian government agency put the overall death toll inside the country above 1,200 as of March 5. Six US service members have been killed, all in a single Iranian strike on a base in Kuwait, along with at least 12 in Israel, 123 in Lebanon, and dozens more across Gulf states.[3][4][5][6][7][8]
